{{Short description|Modification of the random walk model}}
The '''persistent random walk''' is a modification of the [[random walk]] model.

A population of particles are distributed on a line, with constant speed <math>c_0</math>, and each particle's velocity may be reversed at any moment. The reversal time is exponentially distributed as <math>e^{-t/\tau}/\tau</math>, then the population density <math>n</math> evolves according to<ref name=":0">{{Cite journal |last=Weiss |first=George H |date=2002-08-15 |title=Some applications of persistent random walks and the telegrapher's equation |url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0378437102008051 |journal=Physica A: Statistical Mechanics and its Applications |volume=311 |issue=3 |pages=381–410 |doi=10.1016/S0378-4371(02)00805-1 |issn=0378-4371|url-access=subscription }}</ref><math display="block">(2\tau^{-1} \partial_t  + \partial_{tt} - c_0^2 \partial_{xx}) n = 0</math>which is the [[telegrapher's equation]].
